title: Pythagoras and trigonometry in 2D and 3D
cover_sub: Right-angled triangles are everywhere, even inside boxes. Secure Pythagoras and SOH CAH TOA, extend to elevation and bearings, then master lengths and angles in 3D.

levels_long.s: Pythagoras and SOH CAH TOA in one triangle.
levels_long.e: Two-step problems, elevation, bearings, and tampered evidence.
levels_long.m: Lengths and angles inside cuboids and pyramids.

briefing: Pythagoras: in a right-angled triangle, a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse (opposite the right angle). Add to find the hypotenuse; subtract to find a shorter side.
SOH CAH TOA: sin = opphyp, cos = adjhyp, tan = oppadj. In 3D, find a right-angled triangle inside the shape, often using a diagonal of the base first.
method: Find a right-angled triangle and sketch it flat.
Label hyp, opp and adj from the angle you're using.
Two sides, no angle: Pythagoras. An angle involved: SOH CAH TOA.
In 3D, work out the base diagonal first, then use it in a vertical triangle.

example.question: A cuboid measures 3 cm by 4 cm by 12 cm. Find the length of the longest diagonal.
steps: The base is 3 cm by 4 cm. Its diagonal: √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 cm.
The longest diagonal makes a right-angled triangle with the base diagonal (5 cm) and the height (12 cm).

text: A square-based pyramid has a base of side 6 cm. The apex is directly above the centre of the base, and each sloping edge is 7 cm. Find the height of the pyramid.
questions.working: Half the base diagonal is √18 = 4.24. Height √(49 − 18) = √31.
